title: Storm sewer policy and Ayr truck safety
subtitle: Roundabout land expropriation, Swan Street speed limit, Roger Street grant phasing, greenhouse gas report, and deferred agenda items.
overview: The committee recommended adopting an updated Regional Storm Sewer Cost Sharing Policy {{vote:m6}}. Staff said it responds to new provincial approval guidance, was developed with all seven area municipalities, and does not change how costs are shared between partners. The aim is to let storm sewers be replaced and rehabilitated more quickly across the Region.

Through the consent agenda, the committee also recommended phasing payments of a previously approved tax increment grant for 99, 103 and 107 Roger St. in Waterloo, starting expropriation of land for a roundabout at Roseville Road and Edworthy Side Road in North Dumfries, and extending the 50 km/h limit on Swan Street.

Two Ayr residents described truck safety problems in the downtown. A councillor said alternate routes are being studied, but the work will take time. Staff presented the 2022 corporate greenhouse gas inventory, which was received for information.
Because of a hard stop, the committee deferred the rest of its agenda and the Administration and Finance agenda to the April 24 Council meeting {{vote:m7}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council adopt the revised Regional Storm Sewer Cost Sharing Policy dated February 29, 2024 {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Roseville Road and Edworthy Side Road roundabout
decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start expropriation of partial lands and temporary grading easements needed for the roundabout in North Dumfries.
The committee recommended extending the 50 km/h limit on Swan Street to Brant-Waterloo Road by removing the 80 km/h section from the Traffic and Parking By-law.
The committee recommended approving phased payments of the previously approved joint tax increment grant for 99, 103 and 107 Roger St., Waterloo, and authorizing staff to sign the related agreements.
The committee deferred the remaining Planning and Works and Administration and Finance agendas to be dealt with before Council on April 24 {{vote:m7}}.

debate: Delegates from Ayr said large trucks use the downtown, including on sidewalks, and described near-misses, damage and tight turns that force vehicles to back up. They asked for unnecessary truck traffic to be redirected so the core can be safe for children, older residents, cyclists and pedestrians.

Councillor Foxton said Ayr's council had already passed a motion against truck traffic, and that the Region's upgrade of Tresler Road was meant to draw trucks away from the core. A proposed route would use upgraded Brant-Waterloo and Wheatfield roads, but the work will take time.
Councillor Foxton also warned that the Tresler Road roundabout work could push more trucks through Ayr in the short term, and that signs in Paris direct drivers to the Ayr-Paris road.
One councillor asked whether the downtown's original turning radius was designed for today's longer combination trucks, and asked staff to consider this in any review.

On the storm sewer policy, staff said it updates an older policy, was reviewed by all area municipalities, and is reciprocal. No questions were raised. On the greenhouse gas report, a rise in landfill emissions was linked partly to a revised methane potency measure, and no questions followed.
